entries.topic: Homicide over time in Israel and the US; the Arab-community killings

claims.text: Abraham Initiatives (Dec 2025): 252 Arab citizens killed in 218 incidents in 2025, the deadliest year on record; 230 in 2024; 88% shot; over 72% aged 18-40; Herzog: 'These are shocking numbers - an unacceptable situation'; more than 15 killed in early January 2026.

Abraham Initiatives: 244 Arab community members killed in 2023, more than double 2022; about 88% shootings; clearance 10.5% in 2023 (23 cases), 21% in 2022, 19% in 2021; homicides fell 50% in two months after 7 Oct with more police in Arab towns; Bennett government plans NIS 2.4bn policing and NIS 30bn development 'hollowed out'; report blames Ben-Gvir; Comptroller Englman: 'a resounding failure of Israeli governments'.

Maariv 28 Dec 2025: 252 Arab citizens killed in 2025; 23 women, a record; 12 killed in police operations; Israel Police disputed the data, saying it includes offenders killed by police while on their way to kill.

CNN Jan 2026: Arab citizens about 20% of population; 46 killed in 2026 at time of writing; police solved about 15% of homicides in Arab communities vs 65% among Jewish Israelis (Knesset and Eilaf data); Stop the Bleeding funding cut after Ben-Gvir took office; Dec 2025 PMO plan to redirect $70m from Arab economic development to police; Police Commissioner Levi: 'a state of national emergency'; Ben-Gvir: 'There is 20% less murder in the Jewish sector'.

ToI 13 Oct 2026: Abraham Initiatives count 184 killed in Arab community since start of 2026, 156 of them shot; 200 deaths in same period of 2025. Earlier ToI items: 83 by 6 Apr 2026, 30% above same period 2025; 149 by 2 Jul 2026.

Government approved 15 Jul 2026 a Shin Bet role against illegal-weapons smuggling and trade in Arab communities; NIS 497m from the 2021 NIS 30bn 550 plan (NIS 345m Shin Bet, NIS 132.4m police unit); proposed by Netanyahu, Golan, Ben-Gvir; Abraham Initiatives: 'Crime is not terror'; ACRI and Mossawa objected; police solved about 10% of 2025 Arab-community homicides; 156 killed by mid-July 2026.
126 Arab citizens killed in 2021 per Abraham Initiatives (then a record), 62 under 30, 16 women.

Israel Police data (via Association for Freedom of Information): Arab victims 73 (2018), 94 (2019), 110 (2020), 126 (2021), 109 (2022), 222 (2023); 1 Jan 2018-7 Oct 2023: 981 victims, 712 Arab, 214 Jewish, 50 foreign, 5 unknown; Arabs ~21% of population, 73% of victims.

Taub Center Feb 2024: Israel crude homicide rate 1.56 (2019), 1.59 (2020), 1.84 (2021), 1.50 (2022), 3.04 (2023); Arab 4.90 (2019), 11.11 (2023); Jewish/other 0.67 (2019), 0.85 (2023); Arab:Jewish ratio ~4:1 until ~2015, ~10:1 2020-22, 13:1 2023; US 5.40 in 2019; US Black:White ratio ~8:1 pre-COVID; authors call the rise a sign of institutional failure.
Israel Police counts: 135 murders in 2009, 103 homicide victims in 2018 (rate 1.14).

FBI 2025 data (Aug 2026): US homicide rate 4.1 per 100,000, tied with 1955-56 as lowest; murder down 18.1% 2024-25; 2020 homicides up nearly 30%, largest one-year jump; declines continued in first half 2026.
NPR 30 Jun 2026: US rate 6.8 in 2021, up 54% from 4.4 in 2014; murders down 18.7% in first four months of 2026; Canada 1.9.

CCJ Oct 2026: US homicide rate 10.2 in 1980, 4.4 in 2014, 6.6 in 2020, 4.1 in 2025 (60% below 1980); Black victimization rate averaged ~8x White 1976-2025, ~10x in 2020; firearms in 59% (1980s low) to 77% (2021) of homicides; at least 71% each year since 2015.

entries.topic: Gun law, gun ownership, gun deaths and mass shootings in Israel and the US

claims.text: CDC via Pew: 44,447 US gun deaths in 2024; 27,593 suicides (62%), 15,364 homicides (35%); gun death rate 12.8 per 100k (peak 16.3 in 1974); gun homicide rate 4.7 (2024), 6.7 (2021), 7.2 (1974 peak); gun suicide rate 7.6 (record 7.7 in 1977); 76% of homicides by gun in 2024; GVA mass shootings 690 (2021), 645 (2022), 660 (2023), 502 (2024), 510 deaths 2024; FBI active shooter incidents 3 (2000), 61 (2021), 24 (2024); no single agreed definition of mass shooting.

Israel post-Oct 7 reform: ~188,000 licences issued in the year, 365,000 applications; figures of 154,458 (2022) and 315,756 (2024), 'more than doubled', described inconsistently in the article as people 'without a licensed firearm' and 'who had an unlicensed firearm' (wording unclear; not used as a licence-holder count); dozens of communities added to eligible list (list sealed); rescue volunteers and national-service members eligible; temporary national-service staff 8 Oct-2 Dec 2023 issued 23,000 temporary and 15,424 permanent licences; 1,146 suspected of violating criteria; AG halted their work; Lahav 433 investigating; Ben-Gvir's office: murders of women 'occurred with illegal weapons or kitchen knives'.

Firearms Law 1949: 'no person shall possess a firearm, except under license' (s.5); licensing discretionary (s.12), no right to own firearms; thresholds age 21 with service, 27 without, 45 for permanent residents; ~170,000 licences before 7 Oct 2023; 280,000 individually licensed guns in 1998, 147,000 in 2018; ~250,000 applications in first 50 days after 7 Oct, ~1,700 approvals a day in November; goal to triple licence holders; 800+ civilian emergency units; interviews dropped; US reportedly withheld a rifle shipment over concern about settlers.
Small Arms Survey 2018: ~857m civilian firearms worldwide at end of 2017; US ~393.3m, 120.5 per 100 residents.
Small Arms Survey 2017 table: Israel 557,000 civilian firearms, 6.7 per 100.

BSCA signed 25 June 2022: enhanced under-21 checks, $750m state crisis-intervention/red-flag grants, boyfriend loophole partly closed, straw-purchase and trafficking crimes, dealer definition broadened, $13bn+ funding; Bruen (23 June 2022) struck New York's proper-cause requirement and set a text-history-tradition test.

Trump executive order 7 Feb 2025 directed AG Bondi to review federal actions for 'ongoing infringements' of the Second Amendment and present a plan within 30 days, incl. Office of Gun Violence Prevention reports.
8 Sep 2025 Ramot Junction, Jerusalem: two gunmen from the West Bank killed six; a security officer and a civilian shot the attackers; Hamas praised but did not claim.

claims.text: Duke: formerly only combat officers met the service requirement; since 2018 regular service in significant combat positions sufficed; in 2023 any combat service qualifies; 2015 marked the start of measures to increase private gun ownership; thresholds 21 with two years' service (one year for women), 27 without service for citizens, 45 for permanent residents

Ben-Gvir's office: 'no woman has been killed by a weapon provided under the reform'; 'The murders of women occurred with illegal weapons or kitchen knives'; 'in all recent attacks, it was proven that armed citizens are the first to neutralize terrorists'
